post.caption: A nugget that wasn't a nugget. A blast in a Hill End mine in Australia showed a wall of gold. The mine was the Star of Hope on Hawkins Hill, and partners Bernhardt Holtermann and Louis Beyers were credited. It was found around 2 in the morning on October 19, 1872. It was gold in quartz and slate, not a true nugget, and the mass weighed about 285 kilos with about 93 of them gold. Holtermann posed beside it for a photograph. He also hired photographers who left about 3,500 glass negatives, and a garden shed in Chatswood hid them until 1951.
